question:
Which product is formed near the cathode in the given chemical reaction?

2NaCl(aq) + 2H₂O(l) → 2NaOH(aq) + H₂(g) + Cl₂(g)
solution:
The correct answer is __**NaOH, H2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Reactions with NaOH:

 
 
• NaOH (sodium hydroxide) is a strong base that can precipitate hydroxides of various metal cations.
 
• The solubility of the resulting metal hydroxides varies, which can be used to separate the cations.
 
 
 
• Behavior of Cation Pairs with NaOH:
 
 
• Pb2+ forms Pb(OH)2, which is insoluble in excess NaOH.
 
• Al3+ forms Al(OH)3, which is soluble in excess NaOH forming [Al(OH)4]−.
 
• Sn2+ forms Sn(OH)2, which is slightly soluble in excess NaOH.
 
• Cu2+ forms Cu(OH)2, which is insoluble in excess NaOH.
 
• Zn2+ forms Zn(OH)2, which is soluble in excess NaOH forming [Zn(OH)4]2−.
